screens.name: Home — default, omen fixture and transition
screens.evidence: Sheets 34–36 and the push/pull filmstrips show the seated orb, omen, balance and navigation, supported by reported browser layout and contrast checks.
findings: Strengthen the orb’s actionable cue and reduce competition between the parchment question label, Touch the Ball heading and omen.

screens.name: Home — enlarged text and expanded omen policy
screens.evidence: Sheets 34–35 show the enlarged omen policy occupying most of the viewport and the hero outside the expanded-policy view.
findings: Shorten and group the centered attempt-used explanation so the failure, next opportunity and unchanged reading balance scan as one message.

screens.name: Approach — normal, enlarged and transition
screens.evidence: Sheets 3 and 20 show a clear typing action beneath a physically supported orb, while the push/pull filmstrips show background focus changes.
findings: Refine the table’s hard full-width lower edge and its contact with the room so the foreground reads less like a separate rectangular layer.

screens.name: Ask — populated self question, normal, enlarged and transition
screens.evidence: Sheets 4–6 and 20 show the labeled populated question, expansion action, submission button and visible input focus.
findings: Reduce the space and prominence assigned to recipient and disclosure controls so the question remains the unmistakable starting point.

screens.name: Ask — expanded context disclosure
screens.evidence: Sheets 3–4 and 31 show expanded sent-data details pushing the question below the first enlarged viewport, with reported full-disclosure retrieval.
findings: Condense the centered disclosure into short labeled groups so its privacy explanation does not dominate the task at 200%.

screens.name: Ask — populated named-person question
screens.evidence: Sheets 4–5 show About Alex above the matching populated question at normal and enlarged sizes.
findings: Give the recipient-change action a tighter visual grouping with its chevron while keeping the question visually dominant.

screens.name: Recipient selection — populated, corrected and transition
screens.evidence: Sheets 5–6, 21 and 32 show Someone selected, Alex entered and an explicit Use this person action.
findings: Use the same selected-state marker position as other single-choice controls to make selection recognition consistent.

screens.name: Recipient selection — empty and constrained viewport
screens.evidence: Sheets 22 and 32 show the empty-name instruction and disabled action, while the constrained capture ends at the name field.
findings: Keep a visible continuation cue near the constrained name field so users can discover validation and commitment controls below it.

screens.name: Follow-up cards — questions 1, 2 and 3, unselected
screens.evidence: Sheets 11–13 show numbered progress, three radio choices, custom-answer alternatives and disabled Continue or Reveal actions across scales.
findings: Tighten the longest enlarged heading slightly through wording and spacing while preserving the clear choice-to-action sequence.

screens.name: Follow-up cards — selected, focused and pressed
screens.evidence: Sheets 14 and 21 show radio selection, enabled continuation and distinct focus and pressed captures backed by keyboard evidence.
findings: Simplify the multiple nested focus edges while preserving the strong dark outline and gold contrast.

screens.name: Follow-up cards — empty custom answer
screens.evidence: Sheets 13–14 show Your answer, an empty writing area, expansion and the explicit requirement to write before continuing.
findings: Reduce the visual separation between the empty-answer guidance and its disabled action.

screens.name: Follow-up cards — populated custom answer and constrained variants
screens.evidence: Sheets 30–31 show a populated custom response with reachable Reveal and internally scrolling long-answer variants.
findings: Make the internal continuation indicators more visually explicit where enlarged text is cut at the writing-area edge.

screens.name: Question form — constrained short and long drafts
screens.evidence: Sheets 31–32 show retained questions, internal scrolling, expansion and submission within a simulated short viewport.
findings: Keep the continuation caret clearly separated from the fading text so partial lines cannot be mistaken for missing content.

screens.name: Expanded editor — question and custom answer at both viewport heights
screens.evidence: Sheets 24–25 show large writing areas, character counts and Done/Cancel, supported by reported draft-preservation and return-focus checks.
findings: Increase the optical separation between scrolling text and the paper’s top and bottom edges without reducing the available writing space.

screens.name: Age confirmation onboarding
screens.evidence: Sheet 37 shows a concise age question, no-birthday reassurance and two explicit responses at normal and enlarged text.
findings: Give the secondary age response a more clearly bounded interaction area while retaining its lower emphasis.

screens.name: Birthday onboarding — optional empty entry
screens.evidence: Sheet 38 shows optional birthday entry, Skip, a three-field date and responsive two-row reflow at 200%.
findings: Clarify whether Continue with all fields empty has the same result as Skip.

screens.name: Age restriction — onboarding and birthday-edit blocked states
screens.evidence: Sheets 1 and 38–39 show the restriction and birthday-correction route at both scales, with reported under-13 recovery checks.
findings: Shorten the centered supporting explanation to reduce repetitive wrapping beneath the large restriction heading.

screens.name: Birthday correction onboarding
screens.evidence: Sheets 39–40 show required correction fields, Check birthday and a return to the restriction screen.
findings: Compress the enlarged introductory copy so the return action requires less scrolling.

screens.name: Focus onboarding — optional and unselected
screens.evidence: Sheets 2 and 40–41 show four parchment themes, Sun-sign context, Skip focus and normal/enlarged variants.
findings: Reduce the introductory stack slightly so Back remains easier to discover at enlarged text.

screens.name: Focus onboarding — selected
screens.evidence: Sheets 40–41 show Learning & growth checked and the primary action changed to Continue.
findings: Standardize the checkmark placement with recipient and plan selection controls.

screens.name: Birthday editing — populated
screens.evidence: Sheet 72 shows populated date fields, Save, Cancel and collapsed removal, backed by persistence and cancellation evidence.
findings: Give the destructive removal disclosure clearer separation from ordinary cancellation without increasing its prominence.

screens.name: Birthday editing — partial and invalid date
screens.evidence: Sheets 1–2 show field borders and specific missing-day or impossible-date messages at both scales.
findings: Keep the invalid-date explanation compact enough that Save and Cancel remain closely associated with it at 200%.

screens.name: Birth time — initial and optional

screens.name: Birth time — invalid and forgotten confirmation
screens.evidence: Sheets 8–9 show the accepted time range and explicit confirmation that time/place were forgotten while birthday was kept.
findings: Visually distinguish the successful forgetting message from persistent form instructions using a compact centered status group.

screens.name: Birth city — empty and retained draft
screens.evidence: Sheets 6–7 and 70–71 show empty versus Copenhagen entry, disabled versus enabled search and an explicit optional exit.
findings: Place the search instruction closer to the field and keep the provider disclosure visually subordinate.

screens.name: Birth city — unavailable and no-results recovery
screens.evidence: Sheets 7–8 show distinct service-failure and no-match messages, preserved saved-chart guidance and retry/skip routes.

screens.name: Birth city — search results
screens.evidence: Sheets 9–10 show multiple Copenhagen matches with region/country disambiguation and reported actual lookup coverage.
findings: Reduce the repeated search-header footprint after results arrive so more location choices are visible at 200%.

screens.name: Birth profile — saved and retry-success result

screens.name: Planning and research loading

screens.name: Planning and prediction errors

screens.name: Voice unavailable

screens.name: Opening — normal and golden sequence

screens.name: Reveal — expanded more actions

screens.name: Reading details — expanded assumptions

components.name: Wordmark and balance header

components.name: Primary wooden button
components.evidence: Sheets 22 and 30 show focused and pressed wood controls, with supplied target, keyboard and changed-pixel evidence.

components.name: Secondary text action

components.name: Answer choice

components.name: Question input

components.name: Expanded editor modal

components.name: Settings switch

components.name: Omen content

components.name: Sky stars and selected question

components.name: Circle information surface

components.name: History row

components.name: Plan option
components.evidence: Sheets 49–50 show prices and intervals together with selection checks, while supplied evidence covers all three options and radio keyboard behavior.

components.name: Share preview

components.name: Birthday input

components.name: Age confirmation
components.evidence: Sheet 37 shows a direct age question and distinct affirmative and under-age responses without demanding a birthday.
findings: Make the secondary response’s interaction boundary more apparent against the detailed shelf background.

components.name: Focus selection
components.evidence: Sheets 40–41 show wrapping theme labels, a checkmark and a primary action changing from Skip focus to Continue.

components.name: Birth-profile surface
components.evidence: Sheets 10–11 and 72–73 group signs and birth details on parchment with explicit edit/forget routes.
findings: Tighten the profile’s internal action spacing so the enlarged sheet does not crowd out the next account section.

components.name: Birth-details form
components.evidence: Birth-detail sheets cover format guidance, empty entry, retained drafts, invalid time, city results, failures and saved confirmation.
findings: Reduce repeated optional-step and helper copy after the user reaches results or recovery states.

components.name: Named-person control
components.evidence: Recipient sheets show selected Someone, persistent First name labeling, missing-name guidance and populated correction.

components.name: Evidence disclosure
components.evidence: Sheets 26–29 and 52–54 show labeled chevrons, open/closed states, parchment content and return navigation.
findings: Reduce the visual weight of closed wooden disclosures so the expanded evidence remains the dominant surface.

components.name: Export status
components.evidence: Sheets 60–61 distinguish preparation, download started and failure, with supplied real-export, retry and focus-restoration evidence.
findings: Bring each status and its corresponding action into a more compact centered composition.

components.name: Close and Back controls
components.evidence: Sheets 19–20 show separate focused Close and Back controls, supported by reported 44×44 minimum targets and keyboard outlines.
findings: Standardize their placement across modal headers to reduce visual searching between flows.

components.name: Check-in outcome control
components.evidence: Outcome sheets show unselected, selected, unsaved, saved and canceled edits with reported radio-keyboard and persistence coverage.
findings: Keep the live save status close to the outcome choices when they stack vertically.

components.name: Parchment information card
components.evidence: Forecast, history and profile sheets show cut edges and external shadows, while the supplied pixel check confirms shadow pixels beyond the plan card.
findings: Vary contact shading according to the supporting room surface so repeated parchment rectangles feel physically placed rather than uniformly overlaid.

limitations: All grades are provisional browser assessments based on the attached stills, chronological filmstrips and supplied runtime report; I did not independently execute the reported checks.
Equivalent normal, enlarged, transition and outcome variants are grouped explicitly; findings apply to the represented variants rather than unseen screens.

The browser implementation does not meet A≥9 and F≥9 for every screen and meaningful component: centered dense reading, enlarged information hierarchy and some scene integration remain below that threshold.
No demonstrated hard-gate failure is established by this evidence; content below a viewport is not treated as unreachable where the supplied browser report verifies scrolling and action access.
Filmstrips support observations about sampled composition and continuity, not continuous-motion smoothness or frame rate; performance statements come only from the supplied runtime measurements.
Physical iPhone, VoiceOver, native keyboard, tilt, haptics, actual OS sharing and native performance remain unverified and receive no deduction solely for that deferred boundary.
Connected Circles behavior, successful native voice input, real billing and actual notification delivery are not demonstrated; their pictured browser fallback states were evaluated separately.
Fixture forecasts, dense synthetic passages and synthetic source labels do not establish predictive accuracy, source quality or production-copy defects.
Zero reported axe violations and contrast checks support browser accessibility but do not independently establish complete assistive-technology usability.
Painted appearance and sampled layering do not prove independently painted assets, parallax or a continuous three-dimensional camera.
topFixes: Improve centered long-form reading with shorter visual passage groups, stronger section separation and quieter metadata while preserving complete text.
Compact enlarged disclosures, profile sheets, plan terms and invitation introductions so important actions and continuation cues are easier to discover.
Make scrolling-field carets more prominent and separate them from edge fades and partially visible text.
Refine table edges, parchment contact shadows and the Sky window mounting to reduce the remaining pasted-on appearance.
Reduce room brightness/framing changes during destination transitions and soften the golden orb’s geometric halo.
Standardize selection-marker placement, modal navigation placement and secondary-action affordances across flows.
